description_full: Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. research and development, design, manufacturing, and sales of high-speed optical transceivers in China, United States, Singapore, Netherlands, United Kingdom, and Hong Kong. The company offers products, such as a comprehensive portfolio of optical transceivers from 10G to 1.6T, including modules for 400G, 800G, and 1.6T applications; components in optical transceivers and related optical communication equipment, including Transistor Outline Can (TO-CAN) packaged components; and in-vehicle optical transmission solutions for fiber to the vehicle (FTTV) deployment. It also offers services, including the design, research, and manufacturing of high-end optical communication modules and intelligent equipment. The company's product applications include cloud and AI infrastructure, coherent and transport networks, datacom, and telecom. Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. was formerly known as Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. in September 2017. The company was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Longkou, China.

financial_summary: Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. is a large-cap technology business with a $100.6B market cap on $5.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +55% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 29% against a 12% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 33%.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.01× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.8% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
